q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'Deposit' head from a 'Suspense' head of account?

options.A: A deposit is a temporary booking pending classification, whereas a suspense head records a definite liability to an outside party
options.B: Both heads record only the earnings of the Railways awaiting apportionment
options.C: There is no difference between the two; both are remittance heads
options.D: A deposit records an amount held by the Railways which is repayable or adjustable to the party concerned, being a definite liability, whereas a suspense head records a transaction temporarily, pending its adjustment to the final head of account

e: A Deposit head records money held by the Railways for an outside party as a definite liability, repayable or adjustable to that party. A Suspense head is only a temporary parking head used when the final head is not yet known, pending adjustment.

q: The detailed schedules and confirmations obtained in support of the balances under the debt heads of account serve mainly to:

options.A: Fix the budget proportions for the following year
options.B: Substantiate, item by item, the balances recorded in the General Books and to bring out any differences requiring adjustment
options.C: Replace the Trial Balance of the railway
options.D: Determine the earnings to be apportioned among the zonal railways

e: Debt head balances must be supported by detailed schedules and confirmations. These substantiate the General Books balance item by item and bring out differences that need adjustment, so no item remains unverified.

q: For the balances under the debt, suspense and remittance heads to be properly watched, it is necessary that:

options.A: Only the net balance under each head is seen, the details of the items composing it being unnecessary
options.B: The balances are written off and re-created afresh every year
options.C: The debt and suspense balances are merged into a single head
options.D: Each balance is supported by a detailed list of the individual items composing it, so that every item can be pursued and cleared

e: A debt, suspense or remittance balance is meaningful only if it is broken into its individual items. Item-wise lists allow every outstanding item to be pursued, traced and cleared instead of merely watching a net total.

q: A 'proforma adjustment' in Government and railway accounting is best described as an adjustment which:

options.A: Is made for exhibiting results on a comparable or statistical basis, without involving any receipt or payment of cash or altering the cash balance with the Reserve Bank
options.B: Is made by the bank on behalf of the Railways without any advice
options.C: Permanently removes an item from the books without any record
options.D: Converts a revenue item of expenditure into a capital item

e: A proforma adjustment is made only to exhibit results on a comparable or statistical basis. It involves no receipt or payment of cash and does not alter the cash balance with the Reserve Bank.

q:
Consider the following statements about proforma adjustments:
1. A proforma adjustment does not involve any movement of cash between the units concerned.
2. A proforma adjustment is distinct from a regular transfer adjustment, which is posted through the books to the final heads of account concerned.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. A proforma adjustment moves no cash between units, and it differs from a regular transfer adjustment, which is actually posted through the books to the final heads concerned.

q: Adjustments between two departments or accounting units of the Government, in which no cash actually passes and the transaction is settled purely by book entries, are in the nature of:

options.A: Remittances into Banks
options.B: Cash transactions of the Cash & Pay Office
options.C: Receipts of the Public Account
options.D: Departmental (book) adjustments, effected through transfer entries, which leave the cash balance of the Railways with the Reserve Bank unaffected

e: Inter-departmental settlements where no cash passes are departmental or book adjustments. They are effected by transfer entries between the units and leave the Railways cash balance with the Reserve Bank unaffected.

q: An 'Advice of Payment' is sent by an accounting unit which has made a payment on behalf of another unit in order to:

options.A: Report the earnings collected at stations
options.B: Claim a supplementary grant from Parliament
options.C: Advise the bank to stop payment of a cheque
options.D: Intimate the payment to the unit concerned, so that the unit can bring the expenditure to account under its own final head of account

e: An Advice of Payment intimates to the unit concerned that a payment has been made on its behalf. On that advice the unit brings the expenditure to account under its own final head of account.

q:
Consider the following statements about the adjustment of payments made on behalf of another accounting unit:
1. Pending receipt and acceptance of the advice of payment, the amount is held under the appropriate suspense head in the books of the unit on whose behalf the payment was made.
2. On the advice being accepted, the suspense item is cleared by debiting the final head of account to which the expenditure properly belongs.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. Pending receipt and acceptance of the advice, the amount is held under suspense by the unit on whose behalf payment was made; on acceptance, suspense is cleared by debit to the final head.

q: Adjustments between the Central Government and a State Government are finally settled:

options.A: Through the Reserve Bank of India, by book adjustment on the basis of the advices of the accounting authorities concerned, and not by cash passing directly between the two Governments
options.B: By the zonal railways out of the earnings collected at stations
options.C: By writing off the amounts at the close of every year
options.D: Through the Contingency Fund of India in every case

e: Central-State adjustments are settled by the Reserve Bank by book adjustment on the advices of the accounting authorities concerned. No cash passes directly between the two Governments.

q: Amounts remitted from abroad for credit to the Government, which are in the course of settlement and have not yet been credited to the final head of account, are held in the accounts under the:

options.A: Remittance heads, pending final settlement and credit to the head concerned through the Government accounts
options.B: Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: Earnings heads of the Railways
options.D: Works Register of the division concerned

e: Remittances from abroad not yet credited to the final head are in the course of settlement. They are therefore held under the remittance heads pending final settlement through the Government accounts.

q: The periodical monitoring of suspense outstandings at the headquarters of a railway is directed mainly to ensuring that:

options.A: The net balance under each suspense head remains unchanged from year to year
options.B: Fresh items are booked to suspense in larger numbers
options.C: Suspense heads are used for parking funds at the end of the year
options.D: The outstanding items, watched age-wise, are pursued with the units and parties responsible for their clearance and are adjusted to the final heads without avoidable delay

e: Headquarters monitoring of suspense is age-wise pursuit of outstanding items. It ensures items are chased with the responsible units and parties and adjusted to final heads without avoidable delay.

q: The special efforts made before the close of the financial year to clear outstanding suspense items are properly directed to:

options.A: Clearing as many items as possible by tracing them to their final heads, the items which still remain outstanding being carried forward with their full item-wise details
options.B: Writing off all the outstanding items so that the new year opens with no balance
options.C: Netting all the debit items against all the credit items under every head
options.D: Transferring the outstanding items to the Railway Pension Fund

e: Year-end clearance means tracing as many suspense items as possible to their final heads. Items still outstanding are carried forward with full item-wise details, not written off or netted.

q: An item is booked under a suspense head at the close of the financial year merely in order to prevent the lapse of the grant, although its final head of account is known. Such a booking is:

options.A: A regular use of the suspense head
options.B: Improper, a suspense head being operated only where the final head of account cannot be determined at the time of booking, and not as a device to avoid the lapse of a grant
options.C: Permissible with the approval of the dealing assistant
options.D: Treated as a surrender of funds

e: Booking to suspense merely to prevent lapse of a grant is improper. Suspense may be used only when the final head cannot be determined at the time of booking, not as a device to save a grant from lapsing.

q: At the commencement of a new financial year, the balances brought forward in the General Books of a railway are:

options.A: The earnings of the previous year alone
options.B: The balances under the debt, deposit, suspense and remittance heads, representing the assets and liabilities of the railway, the revenue and capital heads of the previous year having been closed
options.C: The budget allotments of the previous year which remained unspent
options.D: No balances at all, every head opening afresh

e: At the start of a new year only debt, deposit, suspense and remittance balances are brought forward, as they represent assets and liabilities. Revenue and capital heads of the previous year are closed and do not open as balances.

q:
Consider the following statements about opening and closing entries in the books of a railway:
1. Opening entries, passed through the Journal, bring into the books of the new year the balances of assets and liabilities outstanding at the close of the previous year.
2. Closing entries close the revenue accounts of the year, the balances under such heads not being carried forward as balances of the new year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. Opening entries through the Journal bring in outstanding asset and liability balances, while closing entries close the revenue accounts, whose balances are not carried forward.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes loans and advances to Government servants from 'Miscellaneous Advances' in railway accounts?

options.A: Loans and advances to Government servants, such as house building advance, are accounted for under the loans heads of account, whereas Miscellaneous Advances is a suspense head for advances of the Railways which are recoverable or adjustable in due course
options.B: Both are suspense heads operated by the Traffic Accounts Office
options.C: Miscellaneous Advances records loans to Government servants, whereas the loans heads record contractors' deposits
options.D: There is no difference between the two in the classification of accounts

e: Loans and advances to Government servants, such as house building advance, are accounted under the loans heads. Miscellaneous Advances is a suspense head for other advances of the Railways recoverable or adjustable in due course.

q:
Consider the following statements about the basis on which railway earnings are accounted:
1. The accounts of the Government are maintained broadly on the cash basis, a payment being accounted when it is actually made.
2. The earnings of the Railways are, however, brought to account on the basis of the traffic booked, the cash in respect of them being realised and remitted thereafter.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. Government accounts are broadly on cash basis, but railway earnings are brought to account on the basis of traffic booked, the cash being realised and remitted thereafter.

q: The budget proportions fixed for expenditure during a year are not necessarily equal period by period, because the proportions are fixed with reference to:

options.A: The pay scales of the staff employed in each period
options.B: The expected pattern of expenditure during the different periods of the year, such as the trend of past actuals and the progress expected on works
options.C: The number of holidays falling in each period
options.D: The earnings of the other zonal railways

e: Budget proportions follow the expected pattern of spending, judged from past actuals trend and expected progress of works. Expenditure is not uniform period to period, so proportions are not equal either.

q: Effective budgetary control by a controlling officer over the allotment placed at his disposal requires him to watch:

options.A: Only the expenditure figures furnished by the Accounts Office after the close of the year
options.B: Only the cash balance held by the Cash & Pay Office
options.C: The suspense balances of the railway as a whole
options.D: Both the expenditure actually booked and the liabilities and commitments incurred against the allotment, progressively during the year

e: Effective budgetary control requires watching both expenditure actually booked and liabilities and commitments incurred against the allotment, progressively during the year, not merely final figures.

q: Funds surrendered by a spending unit out of its allotment:

options.A: Revert to the controlling authority and may be re-allotted by it to other units or heads within the same grant, the surrendering unit having no claim to recall them at will
options.B: Remain at the disposal of the surrendering unit for any other work it chooses
options.C: Are credited to the Development Fund of the Railways
options.D: Require the approval of Parliament before they can be given up

e: Surrendered funds revert to the controlling authority, which may re-allot them to other units or heads within the same grant. The surrendering unit has no right to recall them at will.

q: An error is discovered in an entry already made in the account books of a railway. The correct method of rectification is to:

options.A: Erase the original entry and write the correct entry in its place
options.B: Overwrite the figures in the original entry so that no trace of the error remains
options.C: Destroy the page of the book containing the erroneous entry
options.D: Pass a fresh transfer (journal) entry correcting the error, so that both the original entry and its correction remain traceable in the records

e: Errors are never erased or overwritten in Government accounts. Rectification is by a fresh transfer or journal entry, leaving both the original entry and its correction traceable in the records.

q: The Revenue Account forming part of the annual commercial accounts of the Railways exhibits:

options.A: Only the capital outlay incurred during the year
options.B: The earnings of the year against the working expenses of the year, including the appropriations to the funds charged to revenue, so as to arrive at the net revenue or surplus of the year
options.C: Only the balances under the suspense heads at the close of the year
options.D: The works included in the Works Programme for the following year

e: The Revenue Account sets earnings of the year against working expenses, including appropriations to funds charged to revenue. The balance so arrived at is the net revenue or surplus of the year.

q:
Consider the following statements about the annual commercial accounts of the Railways:
1. The Capital Account exhibits the capital outlay of the Railways and the assets created out of it, as reflected in the Block Account.
2. The Revenue Account exhibits the results of the working of the Railways for the year, in the shape of earnings, working expenses and the surplus or shortfall.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. The Capital Account shows capital outlay and assets created, reflected in the Block Account, while the Revenue Account shows earnings, working expenses and surplus or shortfall for the year.

q: The schedules supporting the Balance Sheet of a railway, in respect of the balances under the debt heads, show in substance that:

options.A: Debit balances, representing amounts recoverable, are in the nature of amounts due to the Railways (debtors), and credit balances, representing amounts payable, are in the nature of amounts due by the Railways (creditors)
options.B: All the balances under the debt heads are in the nature of earnings of the Railways
options.C: The schedules are prepared only for the information of the stations
options.D: No schedules are necessary, as the Balance Sheet shows the gross totals of all the heads together

e: In the Balance Sheet schedules, debt head debit balances are amounts due to the Railways, that is debtors, and credit balances are amounts due by the Railways, that is creditors.

q: The examination of the Demands for Grants by the Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways results in a report which is:

options.A: Binding on the Lok Sabha, which must vote the Demands exactly as recommended by the Committee
options.B: A substitute for the Appropriation Act
options.C: Recommendatory in character, the Demands themselves being voted by the Lok Sabha after the report is presented
options.D: Examined by the Comptroller and Auditor General before the Budget is presented

e: The Standing Committee report on Demands for Grants is only recommendatory. The Lok Sabha itself votes the Demands after the report is presented; the Committee does not bind the House.

q: The amounts specified in the Schedule to an Appropriation Act operate as:

options.A: A mere indication of the expenditure expected, which the executive may exceed freely
options.B: The legal ceiling for each service, expenditure beyond the amount appropriated for a grant requiring regularisation as excess expenditure
options.C: The budget allotment for each division of a railway
options.D: The proportionate allotment for the first part of the year

e: Amounts in the Schedule to an Appropriation Act are the legal ceiling for each service. Spending beyond the appropriated amount is excess expenditure requiring regularisation.

q: A contractor defaults in completing his work and his security deposit, held by the Railways under the 'Deposits' head, is forfeited under the terms of the contract by the competent authority. The forfeited amount is then:

options.A: Retained under the 'Deposits' head permanently as a liability to the contractor
options.B: Paid to the other contractors engaged on the work
options.C: Held under Traffic Suspense till the work is completed by another agency
options.D: No longer a deposit liability, and is credited to the revenue of the Railways

e: Once forfeited by the competent authority, a security deposit ceases to be a liability to the contractor. The amount is therefore credited to the revenue of the Railways.

q: The unspent balance of an imprest held by an officer at the close of the financial year is treated in the accounts as:

options.A: An advance outstanding against the holder, shown as such until he renders an account of the expenditure incurred out of it, and not as expenditure of the year
options.B: Final expenditure of the year, whether or not it has been spent
options.C: A deposit received from the officer
options.D: Part of the earnings of the Cash & Pay Office

e: Unspent imprest money is not expenditure until accounted for. It remains an advance outstanding against the holder until he renders account of the expenditure incurred out of it.

q:
Consider the following statements about liabilities outstanding at the close of a financial year:
1. Under the cash basis of accounting, an item becomes expenditure of a year only when the payment in respect of it is actually made.
2. A liability which has been accepted but remains unpaid at the close of the year is held under 'Demands Payable' pending payment, and does not by itself become booked expenditure of that year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. Under cash basis an item is expenditure only when actually paid; an accepted but unpaid liability is held under Demands Payable and is not booked expenditure of that year.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Journal Book from the Ledger in the books of a railway?

options.A: The Journal records only the earnings of stations, whereas the Ledger records only stores transactions
options.B: The Journal is a book of the executive departments, whereas the Ledger is maintained by the Audit Department
options.C: Both books record the transactions in exactly the same manner and serve the same purpose
options.D: The Journal records the adjustment (transfer) entries in chronological order, entry by entry, whereas the Ledger maintains the classified account for each head of account, from whose balances the Trial Balance is extracted

e: The Journal records adjustment or transfer entries chronologically, entry by entry. The Ledger maintains the classified account for each head, and its balances are used to extract the Trial Balance.

q: In the course of a month, a goods shed collects freight on goods traffic, wharfage charges and demurrage charges. Taken together, these collections are classified in the railway accounts under:

options.A: Passenger earnings
options.B: Goods earnings
options.C: Other Coaching Earnings
options.D: Sundry Other Earnings

e: Freight on goods traffic and the allied goods shed charges of wharfage and demurrage are all classified under Goods earnings in the Traffic Accounts classification.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Tatkal charges collected from passengers form part of the Passenger earnings of the Railways.
2. Receipts from the sale of platform tickets form part of the Passenger earnings of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Tatkal charges are a passenger fare related charge and form part of Passenger earnings, so statement 1 is correct. Platform ticket receipts are not Passenger earnings, so statement 2 is not correct.

q: Measurement books, muster rolls and station returns, prepared in the executive departments and at stations and forming the basis on which the accounts are compiled, are classified in the railway accounting system as:

options.A: General Books
options.B: Subsidiary records
options.C: Initial records
options.D: Records of the Audit Department

e: Measurement books, muster rolls and station returns are the original documents on which accounts are compiled. In railway accounting they are classified as initial records.

q: The daily bank scroll received from the accredited bank shows a payment debit for which no corresponding bill or advice can be traced in the Accounts Office. Pending receipt of the bank's advice and adjustment to the final head, the amount is held under:

options.A: PSB Suspense
options.B: Traffic Suspense
options.C: Demands Payable
options.D: Deposits with Reserve Bank

e: An untraced bank debit in the daily scroll cannot yet be taken to a final head. Pending the bank advice it is held under PSB Suspense, the suspense head for such bank transactions.

q: The apportionment of earnings from luggage traffic carried over more than one railway is dealt with in the Traffic Book in:

options.A: Part B, along with the goods earnings
options.B: Neither part, luggage earnings being never apportioned
options.C: A separate part maintained only for luggage traffic
options.D: Part A, luggage being a part of Coaching earnings

e: Luggage is a coaching service, not goods traffic. Its earnings apportionment is therefore dealt with in Part A of the Traffic Book, which covers Coaching earnings.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The expenses of surveys and investigations for a new line project which is subsequently sanctioned and taken up for construction are treated as part of the capital cost of the work.
2. The expenses of surveys for a proposed work which is ultimately abandoned and not taken up are charged to revenue as ordinary working expenses.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. Survey cost of a project later sanctioned forms part of its capital cost, while survey cost of a project finally abandoned is charged to revenue as ordinary working expenses.

q: The earnest money deposited by tenderers whose tenders are not accepted is, until it is refunded to them, held in the railway accounts under:

options.A: Sundry Other Earnings
options.B: The 'Deposits' head
options.C: Traffic Suspense
options.D: The Capital Fund

e: Earnest money of unsuccessful tenderers is money held for outside parties and refundable to them. Until refunded it is held under the Deposits head as a liability.

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the closing and reporting of the annual accounts of the Railways?

options.A: March (Preliminary) Account Current — March (Final) Account Current — compilation of the Finance Accounts and the Appropriation Accounts — audit and laying before Parliament with the report of the Comptroller and Auditor General
options.B: Appropriation Accounts — March (Preliminary) Account Current — Finance Accounts — March (Final) Account Current
options.C: March (Final) Account Current — March (Preliminary) Account Current — laying before Parliament — compilation of the Finance Accounts
options.D: Finance Accounts — audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General — March (Preliminary) Account Current — March (Final) Account Current

e: The sequence is March Preliminary Account Current, then March Final Account Current, then compilation of Finance and Appropriation Accounts, followed by audit and laying before Parliament with the CAG report.

q:
Consider the following statements about re-appropriation of funds:
1. Re-appropriation can be resorted to for meeting expenditure on a new service, provided savings are available elsewhere within the same grant.
2. Re-appropriation orders in respect of a grant for a financial year can be issued only up to the close of that financial year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 2 is correct. Re-appropriation orders can be issued only up to the close of the financial year, and re-appropriation cannot be used to meet expenditure on a new service.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Railway Pension Fund from the State Railway Provident Fund?

options.A: Both funds are built up from the subscriptions of the staff, and both are held under the debt heads of account
options.B: The Pension Fund is a contributory fund of staff subscriptions, whereas the Provident Fund is fed by appropriations from revenue
options.C: Pension payments are made out of the Provident Fund, whereas provident fund withdrawals are paid out of the Pension Fund
options.D: The Pension Fund is fed by appropriations from revenue and meets the pensionary benefits of staff under the old pension scheme, whereas the Provident Fund is a contributory fund built up from the subscriptions of the staff, its balances being held under the debt heads

e: The Railway Pension Fund is fed by appropriations from revenue and pays pensionary benefits under the old pension scheme. The State Railway Provident Fund is contributory, built from staff subscriptions and held under debt heads.

q: A work is included in the Works Programme (Pink Book) with only a token provision, but the detailed estimate for the work has not yet been sanctioned by the competent authority. The correct course for the executive is to:

options.A: Commence the work, the inclusion in the Pink Book itself amounting to sanction of the work
options.B: Commence the work and obtain the sanction afterwards, as budget provision exists for it
options.C: Await the sanction of the work by the competent authority, a regular allotment and expenditure following only thereafter
options.D: Book the expenditure to a suspense head till the sanction is received

e: Inclusion in the Pink Book with token provision is not sanction of the work. The executive must await sanction by the competent authority; regular allotment and expenditure follow only thereafter.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 'focal point' system from the 'door-step banking' arrangement for station earnings?

options.A: Under the focal point system the bank collects the earnings from the stations itself, whereas under door-step banking the stations remit the earnings to a nominated branch
options.B: Under the focal point system, the earnings of a group of stations are remitted to, and accounted at, nominated focal point branches of the accredited bank, whereas under door-step banking the accredited bank itself collects the earnings from the stations
options.C: Both systems require the stations to remit their earnings directly to the Reserve Bank at Nagpur
options.D: The focal point system applies only to coaching earnings, whereas door-step banking applies only to goods earnings

e: Under the focal point system, earnings of a group of stations are remitted to and accounted at nominated focal point bank branches. Under door-step banking, the accredited bank itself collects earnings from the stations.

q:
Consider the following statements about errors and the Trial Balance:
1. The booking of an item under a wrong head of account, the amount and the side of the entry being correct, does not disturb the agreement of the Trial Balance.
2. The posting of an item to the wrong side of an account in the Ledger disturbs the agreement of the Trial Balance.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. A wrong head with correct amount and side is an error of classification and does not disturb the Trial Balance, while posting to the wrong side does disturb its agreement.

q: Journal vouchers, supporting the transfer (journal) entries in the books of a railway, and the cash vouchers of the Cash & Pay Office are numbered:

options.A: In separate serial series, the journal vouchers and the cash vouchers each having their own series
options.B: In one common serial series for both kinds of vouchers
options.C: Only at the close of the financial year, in a single annual series
options.D: By the Audit Department, in a series common to all the zonal railways

e: Journal vouchers and cash vouchers are numbered in separate serial series. Each class of voucher has its own series for control and traceability.

q: A deposit work executed by the Railways for an outside party is completed and its final cost is found to be less than the amount deposited by the party. The unspent balance refundable to the party is accounted for by:

options.A: Crediting the amount to Sundry Other Earnings
options.B: Crediting the amount to the Capital Fund
options.C: Holding the amount under Traffic Suspense
options.D: Debiting the 'Deposits' head, thereby clearing the liability held under it to that extent

e: Refund of the unspent balance of a deposit work clears the deposit liability to that extent. It is therefore accounted by debiting the Deposits head, not by crediting earnings or a fund.

q: The annual licence fee realised from a private party for the use of railway land for a private siding is classified in the railway accounts under:

options.A: Passenger earnings
options.B: Goods earnings
options.C: Other Coaching Earnings
options.D: Sundry Other Earnings

e: Licence fee for use of railway land for a private siding is a miscellaneous receipt unconnected with passenger, goods or coaching traffic. It is classified under Sundry Other Earnings.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The balances of the State Railway Provident Fund form part of the Public Account of India.
2. The balances accumulated in the Railway Funds lapse at the close of the financial year in the same manner as the unspent balances of grants.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct. State Railway Provident Fund balances form part of the Public Account of India, while Railway Fund balances do not lapse like unspent grants at the close of the year.

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the journey of the earnings collected at a station till they are finally taken to account?

options.A: Credit by the Reserve Bank — remittance by the station — check by the Cash Office — collection at the station
options.B: Collection at the station — credit at the Central Accounts Section of the Reserve Bank — remittance with the Cash Remittance Note — check by the Cash Office
options.C: Collection at the station — remittance daily with the Cash Remittance Note — check of the remittance by the Cash Office or the bank — credit to the Railways' account with the Reserve Bank, the amount remaining as Cash-in-Transit till it is so credited
options.D: Check by the Cash Office — collection at the station — remittance at the close of the year — credit by the Reserve Bank

e: Station earnings are collected, remitted daily with the Cash Remittance Note, checked by the Cash Office or bank, and then credited to the Railways account with the Reserve Bank; till credit they remain Cash-in-Transit.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'Vote of Credit' from an 'Exceptional Grant'?

options.A: A Vote of Credit is taken for a special purpose forming part of the current services of the year, whereas an Exceptional Grant is a blank cheque for an indefinite service
options.B: A Vote of Credit is granted where, on account of the magnitude or the indefinite character of the service, the demand cannot be stated with the usual details, whereas an Exceptional Grant is made for a special purpose which does not form part of the current services of the year
options.C: Both are granted for services forming part of the current financial year and are stated with full details
options.D: A Vote of Credit requires no authorisation by Parliament, whereas an Exceptional Grant is voted by the Lok Sabha

e: A Vote of Credit is taken when, due to magnitude or indefinite character, the demand cannot be stated with usual details. An Exceptional Grant is for a special purpose not forming part of current services of the year.

q: An existing passenger service is substantially extended to serve a new area as a result of a fresh policy decision of the Government. The expenditure involved is treated, for the purposes of parliamentary control over new expenditure, as expenditure on:

options.A: A New Service
options.B: A charged service
options.C: A supplementary service
options.D: A New Instrument of Service

e: Substantial extension of an existing service to a new area due to a fresh policy decision is a New Instrument of Service. It is not a wholly New Service, as the service itself already exists.

q:
Consider the following statements about the construction of a new railway line:
1. The cost of the land acquired for the work is treated as part of the capital cost of the work.
2. The interest on the capital borrowed for the work during its construction period is charged to the working expenses of the year in which it accrues.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct. Land cost is part of the capital cost of a new line, while interest during construction is capitalised to the work and is not charged to working expenses of the year.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 'Classified Abstract' from the monthly 'Account Current' of a zonal railway?

options.A: The Classified Abstract is rendered to the Railway Board, whereas the Account Current is an internal summary of the Accounts Office
options.B: Both are complete monthly accounts rendered to the Railway Board, differing only in their titles
options.C: The Classified Abstract is the head-wise summary of the month's transactions, compiled from the subsidiary books, from which the General Books are posted, whereas the Account Current is the complete monthly account of the railway, compiled from the General Books and rendered to the Railway Board
options.D: The Classified Abstract is prepared by the executive departments, whereas the Account Current is prepared by the Audit Department

e: The Classified Abstract is the head-wise summary of the month compiled from subsidiary books, from which the General Books are posted. The Account Current is the complete monthly account compiled from the General Books and rendered to the Railway Board.

q: Amounts held under the head 'Unpaid Wages', and deposits received from parties, which remain unclaimed beyond the prescribed period are finally:

options.A: Transferred to the Railway Pension Fund
options.B: Credited to the revenue of the Railways as lapsed amounts
options.C: Retained under the respective heads permanently
options.D: Transferred to the Contingency Fund of India

e: Unpaid wages and deposits unclaimed beyond the prescribed period lapse. They are finally credited to the revenue of the Railways as lapsed amounts.

q: A transaction is duly entered in the Cash Book of a railway, but its posting to the account concerned in the Ledger is omitted altogether. The effect of this omission is that:

options.A: The Trial Balance will not agree, the omission being of one aspect only of the transaction
options.B: The Trial Balance will agree, every omission being without effect on it
options.C: The Account Current of the month will automatically stand cancelled
options.D: The transaction will be cleared through the head 'Cheques and Bills'

e: Omitting the Ledger posting of a Cash Book entry omits one aspect of the transaction. The Trial Balance therefore will not agree.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. At the close of the financial year, the officers who operate suspense heads furnish a certificate relating to the review, and the correctness, of the outstanding suspense balances under the heads operated by them.
2. An outstanding item under a suspense head can properly be cleared by netting it against an unrelated credit item appearing under the same head.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct. Officers operating suspense heads certify review and correctness of outstandings at year end, but an item cannot be cleared by netting it against an unrelated credit item under the same head.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the periodical inspection carried out by the Accounts Department from the statutory audit of railway accounts?

options.A: The inspection is conducted by the organisation of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, whereas the statutory audit is conducted by the Accounts Department
options.B: Both the inspection and the statutory audit are conducted by the Accounts Department of the railway
options.C: The inspection extends only to the earnings of stations, whereas the statutory audit extends only to expenditure
options.D: The inspection is an internal arrangement under which the Accounts Department examines the initial records and the accounts offices, whereas the statutory audit is conducted on behalf of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India by an organisation independent of the railway Accounts Department

e: Inspection is an internal Accounts Department examination of initial records and accounts offices. Statutory audit is conducted for the CAG by an organisation independent of the railway Accounts Department.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the treatment of two items of expenditure on station buildings?

options.A: The ordinary repairs and maintenance of an existing station building are charged to the revenue working expenses, whereas the construction of an additional station building is a works (capital) expenditure
options.B: Both the repairs of the existing building and the construction of the additional building are charged to Capital
options.C: Both the items are charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund in all cases
options.D: The repairs of the existing building are charged to Capital, whereas the construction of the additional building is charged to revenue

e: Ordinary repairs and maintenance of an existing station building are revenue working expenses. Construction of an additional station building creates a new asset and is works or capital expenditure.

q: The expenditure booked against a grant exceeds the amount of that grant at the close of the year, while savings are available under another grant of the same year. The excess is regularised by:

options.A: Re-appropriation from the other grant in which the savings are available
options.B: An order of the Railway Board transferring the savings between the grants
options.C: A Demand for an Excess Grant, presented after the excess has been examined by the Public Accounts Committee
options.D: Carrying the excess forward as a charge on the grant of the following year

e: Excess over a grant cannot be met by re-appropriation from another grant. It is regularised by a Demand for Excess Grant, presented after examination by the Public Accounts Committee.

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the settlement of an inter-railway transfer transaction?

options.A: Acceptance by the respondent railway — raising of the Transfer Certificate — matching under E-Recon — examination by the respondent railway
options.B: Raising of the Transfer Certificate by the originating railway — examination by the respondent railway — acceptance of the transfer, or its return with objections — matching under E-Recon and clearance of the outstanding under 'Transfer Railways'
options.C: Matching under E-Recon — raising of the Transfer Certificate — payment of cash by the respondent railway — acceptance by the Railway Board
options.D: Examination by the Railway Board — payment by the respondent railway — raising of the Transfer Certificate — acceptance by the originating railway

e: The originating railway raises the Transfer Certificate, the respondent examines it and accepts it or returns it with objections, and the item is then matched under E-Recon and cleared under Transfer Railways.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Wages and salaries remaining unclaimed beyond the prescribed period are transferred to the Railway Pension Fund.
2. Deposits received from contractors and other parties, remaining unclaimed beyond the prescribed period, are transferred to the Depreciation Reserve Fund.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Neither statement is correct. Unclaimed wages and unclaimed deposits, after the prescribed period, are credited to railway revenue as lapsed amounts, not transferred to the Pension Fund or the Depreciation Reserve Fund.

q: Charges for services rendered by the Railways to an outside party, such as testing and inspection charges, are, pending their realisation from the party, accounted for by:

options.A: Crediting the amount to Sundry Other Earnings at once
options.B: Holding the amount under 'Deposits' as a liability of the Railways
options.C: Debiting the amount to the suspense head 'Demands Recoverable'
options.D: Debiting the amount to the working expenses of the Railways

e: Charges for services rendered to an outside party are amounts due to the Railways pending realisation. They are debited to the suspense head Demands Recoverable until recovered.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Debt Service Fund from the Capital Fund of the Railways?

options.A: The Debt Service Fund is maintained to service the debt obligations arising out of the market borrowings of the Railways and to cushion their repayment, whereas the Capital Fund is used to finance capital works out of the Railways' own internal resources
options.B: The Debt Service Fund finances capital works, whereas the Capital Fund services the market borrowings of the Railways
options.C: Both the funds are maintained only for meeting the pensionary liabilities of the Railways
options.D: The Debt Service Fund is fed by the subscriptions of the staff, whereas the Capital Fund is fed by the safety surcharge on passenger fares

e: The Debt Service Fund services debt obligations from market borrowings and cushions repayment. The Capital Fund finances capital works out of the Railways own internal resources.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Finance Accounts of the Railways are compiled by the Controller General of Accounts in the same manner as the accounts of the other Ministries of the Government of India.
2. The Railways were kept outside the departmentalised system of accounting and compile their own accounts through their own accounts organisation.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 2 is correct. Railways were kept outside the departmentalised accounting system and compile their own accounts through their own accounts organisation, not through the Controller General of Accounts.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the treatment of two works on the permanent way?

options.A: Both the renewal of worn-out track and the doubling of a line are charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.B: The renewal of worn-out track is charged to Capital, whereas the doubling of a line is charged to revenue
options.C: Both the works are charged to the ordinary working expenses of the year
options.D: The renewal of worn-out track with similar material is a renewal chargeable to the Depreciation Reserve Fund, whereas the doubling of a line creates an additional asset and is a capital works expenditure

e: Renewal of worn-out track with similar material is a renewal chargeable to the Depreciation Reserve Fund. Doubling of a line creates an additional asset and is capital works expenditure.

q: The pay of the staff of a railway for the last month of a financial year is actually disbursed in the following month, that is, in the next financial year, no amount having been drawn for it before the close of the year. Under the system of accounting followed, the amount is treated as:

options.A: Expenditure of the year to which the pay relates, the liability having accrued in that year
options.B: Expenditure of the next financial year, in which the payment is actually made
options.C: A charge on the Contingency Fund of India
options.D: An advance under 'Miscellaneous Advances' of the next year

e: Railway accounts follow the cash basis, so pay disbursed in the next financial year is expenditure of that next year, in which payment is actually made, not of the year to which the pay relates.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'IPAS' from 'PFMS'?

options.A: IPAS is a platform of the Government of India for monitoring the flow of funds under its schemes, whereas PFMS is the payroll application of the Railways
options.B: Both are applications maintained by the Reserve Bank of India for Government banking transactions
options.C: IPAS is the integrated application of the Railways for payroll and accounts work, whereas PFMS is the central platform of the Government of India for payment, accounting and monitoring of the flow of Government funds, including releases under Government schemes
options.D: IPAS is used for the apportionment of earnings among the zonal railways, whereas PFMS is used for the reservation of passenger accommodation

e: IPAS is the Railways integrated payroll and accounts application. PFMS is the Government of India central platform for payment, accounting and monitoring of fund flow, including scheme releases.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Charges for terminal services rendered at the originating or terminating station are retained by the railway which renders the service and are not apportioned among the railways.
2. Sundry Other Earnings are apportioned among the zonal railways in proportion to the distance over which the traffic connected with them is carried.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct. Terminal charges are retained by the railway rendering the service and are not apportioned; Sundry Other Earnings are likewise not apportioned on a distance basis as stated in statement 2.

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the passing and payment of a bill in a zonal railway?

options.A: Payment by the Cash & Pay Office — preparation of the bill by the executive — internal check by the Accounts Office — stamping of the voucher as 'Paid'
options.B: Internal check by the Accounts Office — preparation of the bill by the executive — payment by the Cash & Pay Office — compilation in the General Books
options.C: Preparation of the bill by the executive — payment by the Cash & Pay Office — internal check by the Accounts Office — stamping of the voucher as 'Paid'
options.D: Preparation of the bill by the executive, with the allocation shown on it — internal check and passing of the bill by the Accounts Office — payment by the Cash & Pay Office — stamping and cancellation of the paid voucher — compilation of the transaction through the Classified Abstract into the General Books

e: A bill is prepared by the executive with allocation, internally checked and passed by Accounts, paid by the Cash and Pay Office, the voucher is stamped and cancelled as paid, and the transaction is compiled through the Classified Abstract into the General Books.

q: Reservation fees, superfast supplementary charges and Tatkal charges collected from passengers are together classified in the railway accounts under:

options.A: Goods earnings
options.B: Sundry Other Earnings
options.C: Passenger earnings
options.D: Other Coaching Earnings

e: Reservation fees, superfast supplementary charges and Tatkal charges are all charges linked to passenger fares. They are classified under Passenger earnings.

q: The consolidated Finance Accounts of the Indian Railways as a whole are compiled:

options.A: By the Controller General of Accounts, from the Pay and Accounts Offices of the Ministries
options.B: By the Railway Board, from the Account Currents rendered by the zonal railways and the other accounting units
options.C: By the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, from the station balance sheets
options.D: By each zonal railway separately, for its own portion of the accounts

e: The Railway Board compiles the consolidated Finance Accounts of Indian Railways as a whole from the Account Currents rendered by zonal railways and other accounting units.

q:
Consider the following statements about the appropriations to the Railway Funds:
1. The appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund is charged to the working expenses of the Railways as provided in the Budget, whether or not there is a surplus.
2. The appropriation to the Capital Fund is made out of the surplus (net revenue) of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. Appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund is charged to working expenses as budgeted, while appropriation to the Capital Fund is made out of the surplus or net revenue.

q: Rent realised for the display of advertisement hoardings on railway land, and rent realised from the leasing of railway premises to outsiders, are both classified in the railway accounts under:

options.A: Passenger earnings
options.B: Goods earnings
options.C: Other Coaching Earnings
options.D: Sundry Other Earnings

e: Rent from advertisement hoardings on railway land and rent from leasing railway premises to outsiders are miscellaneous non-traffic receipts. Both are classified under Sundry Other Earnings.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Works Register from the Works Programme (Pink Book)?

options.A: The Works Register is a document of the Railway Board listing the approved works, whereas the Pink Book is a register of the Accounts Office
options.B: Both are registers maintained in the Accounts Office for recording the expenditure on works
options.C: The Works Register lists the works approved for the year with their budget provision, whereas the Pink Book records the expenditure incurred on each work
options.D: The Works Register is maintained in the Accounts Office and records, work-wise, the expenditure incurred against the sanctioned estimates, whereas the Pink Book is the Works Programme document listing the works approved for inclusion in the year, with the provision made for them

e: The Works Register is maintained in the Accounts Office and records work-wise expenditure against sanctioned estimates. The Pink Book is the Works Programme listing works approved for the year with provision made for them.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Zero-Based Budgeting from the incremental method of budgeting?

options.A: Under Zero-Based Budgeting, the provision for every scheme is obtained by adding a fixed percentage to the previous year's figures, whereas the incremental method requires every scheme to be justified afresh
options.B: Both the methods require every scheme, new as well as continuing, to be justified afresh from a zero base
options.C: Under Zero-Based Budgeting, every programme or scheme, including a continuing one, has to be justified afresh from a zero base, whereas under the incremental method the estimates are built up by adding to the level of expenditure of the past
options.D: Zero-Based Budgeting is applied only to the earnings budget, whereas the incremental method is applied only to the works budget

e: Under Zero-Based Budgeting every programme, including a continuing one, must be justified afresh from a zero base. The incremental method merely builds on the past level of expenditure.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Liability Register from the Budget Register maintained in the Accounts Office?

options.A: The Liability Register records the budget allotments as modified by re-appropriation, whereas the Budget Register records the commitments incurred against the allotments
options.B: The Liability Register records the liabilities and commitments incurred against the allotments, so that the funds required for them are kept in view, whereas the Budget Register records the allotments, as modified by re-appropriation, against which the expenditure is watched
options.C: Both the registers record only the balances outstanding under the suspense heads of account
options.D: The Liability Register is maintained by the executive departments, whereas the Budget Register is maintained by the Audit Department

e: The Liability Register records liabilities and commitments incurred against allotments so funds for them are kept in view. The Budget Register records allotments, as modified by re-appropriation, against which expenditure is watched.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Budget Register from the Works Register maintained in the Accounts Office?

options.A: The Budget Register records, work-wise, the expenditure incurred on each sanctioned work, whereas the Works Register records the allotments under each head of account
options.B: The Budget Register records the allotments under each head of account, as modified by re-appropriation, and the expenditure watched against them, whereas the Works Register records, work-wise, the expenditure incurred on each sanctioned work against its sanctioned estimate
options.C: Both the registers record only the balances outstanding under the suspense heads of account
options.D: The Budget Register is maintained by the executive departments, whereas the Works Register is maintained by the Audit Department

e: The Budget Register records allotments under each head, as modified by re-appropriation, and expenditure watched against them. The Works Register records work-wise expenditure on each sanctioned work against its estimate.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Rolling Stock Programme from the Machinery and Plant Programme of the Railways?

options.A: The Rolling Stock Programme deals with the acquisition and renewal of locomotives, coaches, wagons and other rolling stock, whereas the Machinery and Plant Programme deals with the procurement and replacement of machinery and plant required for workshops and the open line
options.B: The Rolling Stock Programme deals with the procurement of machinery and plant, whereas the Machinery and Plant Programme deals with the acquisition of rolling stock
options.C: Both the programmes deal only with the renewal and replacement of track
options.D: The Rolling Stock Programme is a programme of the stores department, whereas the Machinery and Plant Programme is a programme of the traffic department

e: The Rolling Stock Programme covers acquisition and renewal of locomotives, coaches, wagons and other rolling stock. The Machinery and Plant Programme covers machinery and plant for workshops and the open line.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Depreciation Reserve Fund from the Development Fund of the Railways?

options.A: The Depreciation Reserve Fund is fed out of the surplus of the Railways, whereas the Development Fund is charged to the working expenses
options.B: Both the funds are fed by appropriations charged to the working expenses of the Railways
options.C: The Depreciation Reserve Fund is fed by appropriations charged to the working expenses and is used for renewals and replacements of assets, whereas the Development Fund is fed by appropriations out of the surplus (net revenue) and is used for passenger amenities and other improvement and welfare works
options.D: The Depreciation Reserve Fund is used for the construction of new lines, whereas the Development Fund is used for renewals and replacements

e: The Depreciation Reserve Fund is fed by appropriations charged to working expenses and finances renewals and replacements. The Development Fund is fed out of surplus and finances passenger amenities and improvement and welfare works.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Revised Estimates from the Final Modification Estimates?

options.A: Both the Revised Estimates and the Final Modification Estimates are prepared in January of the financial year
options.B: The Revised Estimates are voted by Parliament, whereas the Final Modification Estimates are not
options.C: The Revised Estimates are the final review of the year leading to the Final Grant, whereas the Final Modification Estimates are prepared in September
options.D: The Revised Estimates, prepared in September, re-estimate the receipts and expenditure of the current year and frame the Budget Estimates of the next year, whereas the Final Modification Estimates, carried out in January, are the final review of the current year's estimates leading to the Final Grant

e: Revised Estimates, prepared in September, re-estimate the current year and frame next year Budget Estimates. Final Modification Estimates in January are the final review of the current year leading to the Final Grant.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a Supplementary Grant from re-appropriation of funds?

options.A: A Supplementary Grant is an additional grant voted by Parliament which increases the total grant for a service, whereas re-appropriation is a transfer of funds within the same grant from one head to another which leaves the total grant unchanged and requires no vote of Parliament
options.B: A Supplementary Grant is a transfer of funds within a grant, whereas re-appropriation is an additional grant voted by Parliament
options.C: Both a Supplementary Grant and re-appropriation increase the total grant voted by Parliament
options.D: A Supplementary Grant requires no authorisation by Parliament, whereas re-appropriation is voted by the Lok Sabha

e: A Supplementary Grant is additional provision voted by Parliament, increasing the total grant for a service. Re-appropriation only transfers funds within the same grant, leaving its total unchanged and requiring no vote.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Railway Safety Fund from the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh?

options.A: The Railway Safety Fund is the later assured safety fund, whereas the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh is fed by the safety surcharge on passenger fares
options.B: The Railway Safety Fund is the earlier fund, fed by the safety surcharge on passenger fares and a share of the cess on petrol and diesel, and used for works of road safety at level crossings and road bridges, whereas the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh is the later assured safety fund used for safety works, including renewals and replacements of track, bridges and signalling assets
options.C: Both the funds are fed by the subscriptions of the railway staff
options.D: The Railway Safety Fund is used for renewals of rolling stock alone, whereas the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh is used for passenger amenities

e: The Railway Safety Fund is the earlier fund, fed by the safety surcharge on fares and a share of petrol and diesel cess for level crossing and road bridge safety works. Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh is the later assured fund for safety works including track, bridge and signalling renewals.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'Remittances into Banks' from 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' in the railway accounts?

options.A: Both the heads represent the balance actually held to the credit of the Railways with the Reserve Bank of India
options.B: 'Remittances into Banks' represents the balance held with the Reserve Bank, whereas 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' represents remittances awaiting credit by the bank
options.C: 'Remittances into Banks' represents amounts remitted into the bank which are still awaiting credit by the bank, whereas 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' represents the balance actually held to the credit of the Railways with the Reserve Bank
options.D: 'Remittances into Banks' is a head of the earnings accounts, whereas 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' is a suspense head for traffic transactions

e: Remittances into Banks are amounts remitted into the bank but still awaiting credit by it. Deposits with Reserve Bank is the balance actually held to the credit of the Railways with the Reserve Bank.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 'Final Grant' from the 'Final Appropriation' in the railway accounts?

options.A: The Final Grant relates to expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, whereas the Final Appropriation relates to voted expenditure
options.B: Both the expressions mean the original grant as voted by Parliament at the beginning of the year
options.C: The Final Grant is the budget allotment communicated to the divisions, whereas the Final Appropriation is the allotment communicated to the stations
options.D: The Final Grant is the final amount of the voted provision for a service after taking into account supplementary grants and surrenders, whereas the Final Appropriation is the corresponding final amount for expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India

e: The Final Grant is the final voted provision for a service after supplementary grants and surrenders. The Final Appropriation is the corresponding final amount for expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'token grant' from a Supplementary Grant?

options.A: A token grant is a nominal grant taken to obtain the approval of Parliament for a new service when the funds for it can be found by re-appropriation within the grant, whereas a supplementary grant is taken when the provision already made for a service is found insufficient and additional funds are required
options.B: A token grant is taken when the provision for a service is insufficient, whereas a supplementary grant is taken for a new service whose funds are found by re-appropriation
options.C: Both a token grant and a supplementary grant are taken only at the close of the financial year
options.D: A token grant requires no approval of Parliament, whereas a supplementary grant is approved by the Railway Board alone

e: A token grant is a nominal grant to obtain Parliament approval for a new service when funds can be found by re-appropriation. A supplementary grant is taken when existing provision is insufficient and additional funds are needed.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Cash Book from the Journal Proper in the books of a railway?

options.A: The Cash Book records only the adjustment entries of a railway, whereas the Journal Proper records all cash receipts and payments
options.B: The Cash Book records all cash receipts and payments and also serves as the ledger account for cash, whereas the Journal Proper records those entries which find no place in any other subsidiary book, such as opening, closing and adjustment entries
options.C: Both the Cash Book and the Journal Proper are maintained by the executive departments and not by the Accounts Office
options.D: The Cash Book is a General Book, whereas the Journal Proper is the principal book from which the Trial Balance is extracted

e: The Cash Book records all cash receipts and payments and itself serves as the ledger account for cash. The Journal Proper records entries finding no place in any other subsidiary book, such as opening, closing and adjustment entries.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'internal check' from 'inspection' in the railway accounts organisation?

options.A: Internal check is conducted by the organisation of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, whereas inspection is conducted by the Cash & Pay Office
options.B: Both internal check and inspection are parts of the statutory audit of the railway accounts
options.C: Internal check is the check applied in the Accounts Office to transactions as they are presented and passed, whereas inspection is the periodical examination, by the Accounts Department, of the initial records and working of an accounts or executive office
options.D: Internal check extends only to the earnings of stations, whereas inspection extends only to the balances under the suspense heads

e: Internal check is the check applied in the Accounts Office to transactions as presented and passed. Inspection is the periodical examination by the Accounts Department of initial records and working of an office.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Objectionable Item Register from the Suspense Register maintained in the Accounts Office?

options.A: The Objectionable Item Register watches the items outstanding under the suspense heads, whereas the Suspense Register watches the items held under objection in internal check
options.B: Both the registers are maintained for watching the progress of expenditure against the budget allotments
options.C: The Objectionable Item Register is a register of the Traffic Accounts Office alone, whereas the Suspense Register is a register of the Audit Department
options.D: The Objectionable Item Register watches items of expenditure or receipts held under objection during internal check till they are regularised, whereas the Suspense Register watches, item-wise, the amounts outstanding under a suspense head till they are cleared to the final heads of account

e: The Objectionable Item Register watches items held under objection in internal check till regularised. The Suspense Register watches item-wise amounts outstanding under a suspense head till cleared to final heads.

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the authorisation of expenditure through a Vote on Account?

options.A: Vote on Account voted by the Lok Sabha — Appropriation (Vote on Account) Act passed — expenditure incurred for the initial part of the year — Demands for Grants for the full year voted and the main Appropriation Act passed
options.B: Main Appropriation Act passed — Vote on Account voted by the Lok Sabha — expenditure incurred for the initial part of the year — Demands for Grants voted
options.C: Expenditure incurred for the initial part of the year — Vote on Account voted by the Lok Sabha — Demands for Grants voted — Appropriation (Vote on Account) Act passed
options.D: Demands for Grants for the full year voted — Vote on Account voted by the Lok Sabha — main Appropriation Act passed — Appropriation (Vote on Account) Act passed

e: A Vote on Account is first voted by the Lok Sabha and the Appropriation (Vote on Account) Act is passed, enabling expenditure for the initial part of the year, after which the full Demands are voted and the main Appropriation Act passed.

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the framing of the Earnings Budget of a zonal railway?

options.A: Scrutiny by the Accounts Department — inclusion in the Budget presented to Parliament — estimates framed by the executive departments — consolidation by the Railway Board
options.B: Estimates framed by the executive (operating and commercial) departments on the basis of the traffic expected — scrutiny by the Accounts Department — consolidation at the zonal headquarters and by the Railway Board — inclusion in the Budget presented to Parliament
options.C: Inclusion in the Budget presented to Parliament — estimates framed by the executive departments — consolidation by the Railway Board — scrutiny by the Accounts Department
options.D: Consolidation by the Railway Board — scrutiny by the Accounts Department — estimates framed by the executive departments — inclusion in the Budget presented to Parliament

e: Earnings estimates are framed by executive departments from expected traffic, scrutinised by Accounts, consolidated at zonal headquarters and by the Railway Board, and then included in the Budget presented to Parliament.

q: Stores are purchased by a division for immediate use on a specific sanctioned work and are not taken into the stock of a stores depot. In the accounts, the cost of such stores is:

options.A: Debited to the head 'Stores Suspense' in all cases, whether or not the stores enter stock
options.B: Held under the head 'Miscellaneous Advances' till the work is completed
options.C: Charged directly to the head of account of the work concerned, the head 'Stores Suspense' being operated only for stores taken into stock
options.D: Credited to Sundry Other Earnings of the Railways

e: Stores bought for immediate use on a specific work and not taken into depot stock are charged directly to that work head. Stores Suspense is operated only for stores taken into stock.

q: A private siding owned by an outside party is maintained by the Railways at the cost of the owner, and the charges for the maintenance have not yet been recovered from the owner. Pending recovery, the amount is accounted for by:

options.A: Crediting the amount to Sundry Other Earnings at once
options.B: Charging the amount finally to the ordinary working expenses of the Railways
options.C: Holding the amount under the 'Deposits' head as a liability of the Railways
options.D: Debiting the amount to the suspense head 'Demands Recoverable'

e: Maintenance charges of a private siding recoverable from its owner are amounts due to the Railways pending recovery. They are debited to the suspense head Demands Recoverable.

q: During the physical verification of stores in a depot, the stores actually found exceed the book balance, and the excess is not immediately explained. Pending investigation and regularisation, the value of the excess is adjusted in the accounts through:

options.A: The Stock Adjustment Account
options.B: Sundry Other Earnings of the Railways
options.C: The Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: The head 'Traffic Suspense'

e: Excess stores found on physical verification, pending investigation and regularisation, are adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account, which deals with differences between physical and book stock.

q: A tenderer whose tender has been accepted fails to take up the contract, and his earnest money deposit is forfeited by the competent authority under the terms of the tender. The forfeited amount is then:

options.A: Retained under the 'Deposits' head permanently as a liability to the tenderer
options.B: Credited to the revenue of the Railways, the amount no longer being a deposit liability
options.C: Transferred to the Capital Fund of the Railways
options.D: Refunded to the tenderer at the close of the financial year

e: Forfeited earnest money of a tenderer who fails to take up the contract ceases to be a deposit liability. It is credited to the revenue of the Railways.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Wages and salaries drawn before the close of a month but remaining undisbursed are credited to the head 'Unpaid Wages', pending disbursement to the staff entitled to them.
2. When the amount so held is afterwards disbursed, it is debited to the head 'Unpaid Wages' and is not charged afresh to the working expenses of the month of disbursement.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. Undisbursed wages drawn are credited to Unpaid Wages pending disbursement, and later payment is debited to Unpaid Wages without being charged afresh to working expenses.

q: The Annual Financial Statement (Union Budget) is presented to Parliament:

options.A: In the Rajya Sabha first, and thereafter in the Lok Sabha
options.B: In both Houses simultaneously by the President of India
options.C: Only in the Lok Sabha, a copy never being laid before the Rajya Sabha
options.D: In the Lok Sabha by the Finance Minister, a copy of it being thereafter laid before the Rajya Sabha

e: The Annual Financial Statement is presented in the Lok Sabha by the Finance Minister under Article 112. A copy is thereafter laid before the Rajya Sabha.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 150 of the Constitution, the accounts of the Union and of the States are kept in the form prescribed by the President on the advice of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
2. The List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, which gives effect to that form for classification purposes, is issued by the Controller General of Accounts.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct as keyed. Article 150 provides that Union and State accounts are kept in the form prescribed by the President on the advice of the CAG, and the List of Major and Minor Heads gives effect to that classification.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a Transfer Certificate from a TWFA advice in inter-railway transfer transactions?

options.A: A Transfer Certificate is used for a transfer involving no financial effect, whereas a TWFA advice is used to raise a debit against the respondent railway
options.B: A Transfer Certificate is used to intimate a transfer transaction which has a financial effect, that is, a debit or a credit, to the respondent railway, whereas a TWFA advice is used for a transfer transaction which involves no financial effect
options.C: Both a Transfer Certificate and a TWFA advice involve an actual remittance of cash between the railways
options.D: A Transfer Certificate is issued by the Railway Board alone, whereas a TWFA advice is issued by the stations

e: A Transfer Certificate intimates a transfer with financial effect, a debit or credit, to the respondent railway. A TWFA advice, transfer without financial adjustment, is used where the transfer has no financial effect.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Every entry in the Journal Book of a railway must be supported by a Journal Voucher duly signed by an Accounts Officer.
2. A transfer entry may be passed on the verbal instructions of the dealing assistant, without any Journal Voucher.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 2 only
options.C: 1 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct. Every Journal entry must be supported by a Journal Voucher signed by an Accounts Officer; a transfer entry cannot be passed merely on verbal instructions of a dealing assistant.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Consolidated Fund of India from the Public Account of India in respect of disbursements?

options.A: Disbursements out of both the Consolidated Fund of India and the Public Account of India require appropriation by Parliament
options.B: Withdrawals from the Consolidated Fund of India do not require appropriation, whereas disbursements out of the Public Account of India do
options.C: The Public Account of India is a part of the Consolidated Fund of India, and the same rule of appropriation applies to both
options.D: Withdrawals from the Consolidated Fund of India can be made only under appropriation made by law, whereas disbursements out of the Public Account of India, in which the Government holds moneys in trust, do not require appropriation by Parliament

e: Under Articles 266 and 283, withdrawals from the Consolidated Fund can be made only under appropriation by law. Public Account moneys are held in trust, so their disbursements do not require appropriation by Parliament.

q: A work of passenger amenities is financed from Capital (Gross Budgetary Support) instead of from the Development Fund. In the classification of accounts, the work is classified:

options.A: Under the Plan Head for passenger amenities, the source of finance being shown as Capital in the allocation of the work
options.B: Under the subdivision of the Development Fund in all cases, the fund alone determining the classification
options.C: Under Sub-Major Head 11 of Major Head 3002 as a revenue work
options.D: Under a separate Plan Head created for works financed from Gross Budgetary Support

e: Works classification is by Plan Head, and the source of finance does not change that classification. A passenger amenity work financed from Capital is classified under its Plan Head with Capital shown as the source in the allocation.
